messages.author: 118ad936abe03634
messages.subject: Simulate Besag Spatial Effects
parts:
Hi there, I am simulating spatial effects following the code of the besagproper.pdf of the inla.doc("besagproper") documentation.

In the notes in the last part of the documentation says that if d = 0 and the parameter rankdef=1 is set, then this model corresponds to the besag model.

The problem is that when I use d = 0 I get an error in the chol(Q) line. How could I simulate besag model effects?

library(INLA)
## pick a graph
graph = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
g = inla.read.graph(graph)
## we will use replicated samples in our testing
nrep = 5
## make life easy; use dense matrix algebra
d = 0
tau = 1.0
Q = matrix(0, g$n, g$n)
diag(Q) = tau * (d + g$nnbs)
for(i in 1:g$n) {
  if (g$nnbs[i] > 0) {
    Q[i, g$nbs[[i]]] = -tau
    Q[g$nbs[[i]], i] = -tau
  }
 }
 R = chol(Q) ## 'chol' returns the upper triangular
 Error in chol.default(Q) : 
  the leading minor of order 544 is not positive definite

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Simulate Besag Spatial Effects
parts:
exactly, in that case the prec matrix Q is not pos definite.
you can use the Algorithms in chapter 2 in the GMRFbook (Alg 2.6),
or you can simply use

inla.qsample

just add a small eps on the diagonal of Q, and add the sum-to-zero
constraint
